evidence.quote: by and between Redwood Peak Construction Co., a California corporation
evidence.rationale: Named as Contractor in the preamble.

evidence.quote: and Precision Roofing & Sheet Metal, a California corporation
evidence.rationale: Named as Subcontractor in the preamble.

evidence.quote: with the City of Santa Rosa, a California
evidence.rationale: The City of Santa Rosa is defined as Owner under the Prime Contract.

evidence.quote: the project known as Fire Station 5 Replacement, located at 2290
evidence.rationale: Project name stated in the recitals.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California.
evidence.rationale: Section 15.1 is the governing-law clause.

evidence.quote: The parties confirm in writing that Section 6.3, as amended by this Amendment No. 1, remains a pay-when-paid provision
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 and Amendment No. 1 call this a pay-when-paid provision. Payment falls due a stated number of days after Owner Payment, and there is no express condition precedent.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for that work
evidence.rationale: Amendment No. 1 (A1.1/A1.2) replaces the original 10-day period in Section 6.3 with 7 days. A1.3 says the Amendment controls over the Subcontract.

evidence.quote: the payment period of seven (7) days after Owner Payment replaces the ten (10) day period stated in the original Subcontract for all progress payments
evidence.rationale: A specific period is written in the signed Amendment, and the parties expressly confirm it in writing.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall retain five percent (5%) of the amount of each progress payment due to Subcontractor as retainage.
evidence.rationale: 5% equals 500 basis points.

release_condition.value: upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner

evidence.quote: Retainage shall be released to Subcontractor upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states the release triggers. Section 7.3 adds further delivery conditions, including evidence satisfactory to Contractor.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay the retainage to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both of these conditions have been satisfied.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2. Amendment A1.3 confirms the retainage release period is unchanged.

evidence.quote: With each application for progress payment, Subcontractor shall submit a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested, executed by Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2.

evidence.quote: Within five (5) days after receiving each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment for the amount actually paid.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.3.

evidence.quote: conditional waivers and releases from each of its lower-tier subcontractors and suppliers whose work or materials are included in that application
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4 requires conditional and unconditional lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: shall be in the statutory forms prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.5.

evidence.quote: Contractor may back charge Subcontractor for, and set off against any amount due or to become due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract, all Backcharges incurred by Contractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment otherwise due Subcontractor an amount sufficient to cover the cost of correcting defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work that has not been remedied.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1. Section 9.3 also allows withholding for claims.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall not be obligated to pay for any materials or equipment stored on or off the Project site.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 expressly excludes payment for stored materials.

anomalies.description: Amendment No. 1 changes the progress payment period from 10 days to 7 days after Owner Payment, and applies it to any application pending on February 9, 2026. Section 6.3 in the original body still reads 10 days, so payment systems must use the amended 7-day period.

evidence.quote: Section 6.3 of the Subcontract is amended by deleting the words "within ten (10) days after Contractor's receipt of Owner Payment" and replacing them with "within seven (7) days after Contractor's receipt of Owner Payment."
evidence.rationale: Amendment No. 1 changes the progress payment period from 10 days to 7 days after Owner Payment, and applies it to any application pending on February 9, 2026. Section 6.3 in the original body still reads 10 days, so payment systems must use the amended 7-day period.

anomalies.description: The retainage release period stays at 10 days while progress payments moved to 7 days. These are two different day counts in the same contract.

evidence.quote: The retainage release period stated in Section 7.2 is not changed by this Amendment.
evidence.rationale: The retainage release period stays at 10 days while progress payments moved to 7 days. These are two different day counts in the same contract.

anomalies.description: Payment falls due only after Owner Payment, and no outside date is stated for payment if Owner does not pay.

evidence.quote: obligation to pay each progress payment falls due a stated number of days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for the Subcontract Work included in that payment.
evidence.rationale: Payment falls due only after Owner Payment, and no outside date is stated for payment if Owner does not pay.

anomalies.description: Termination-for-convenience payments are limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner. This places the risk of owner non-payment on Subcontractor for those amounts.

evidence.quote: to the extent Contractor recovers those amounts from Owner, with no allowance for anticipated profit on unperformed work.
evidence.rationale: Termination-for-convenience payments are limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner. This places the risk of owner non-payment on Subcontractor for those amounts.

anomalies.description: Retainage release depends on Owner's release of retention. It also requires evidence 'satisfactory to Contractor', which is a discretionary trigger.

evidence.quote: (d) evidence satisfactory to Contractor that all lower-tier claimants have been paid in full.
evidence.rationale: Retainage release depends on Owner's release of retention. It also requires evidence 'satisfactory to Contractor', which is a discretionary trigger.

anomalies.description: Contractor may withhold Article 9 amounts from retainage.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from retainage any amounts that Contractor is entitled to withhold under Article 9, subject to applicable law.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold Article 9 amounts from retainage.

anomalies.description: Contractor may withhold 125% of the amount of a stop payment notice or bond claim not released within 10 days.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from amounts due Subcontractor an amount equal to one hundred twenty-five
evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold 125% of the amount of a stop payment notice or bond claim not released within 10 days.

anomalies.description: Contractor may withhold the entire next progress payment until the unconditional waiver for the prior payment is received.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold Subcontractor's next progress payment until the unconditional waiver for the prior payment is received.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold the entire next progress payment until the unconditional waiver for the prior payment is received.

anomalies.description: Broad additional withholding rights cover lower-tier claims, missing certified payroll, damage to others' work, and penalties.

evidence.quote: Contractor may also withhold amounts reasonably necessary to protect Contractor against: (a) unpaid claims of Subcontractor's lower-tier subcontractors, suppliers, or laborers; (b) Subcontractor's failure to submit required certified payroll records
evidence.rationale: Broad additional withholding rights cover lower-tier claims, missing certified payroll, damage to others' work, and penalties.

anomalies.description: Contractor may unilaterally adjust the amount of Subcontractor's application based on its own evaluation.

evidence.quote: Contractor may adjust Subcontractor's application to reflect Contractor's good-faith evaluation of the percentage of work actually completed.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may unilaterally adjust the amount of Subcontractor's application based on its own evaluation.
